title: ‘ZERO’ percent chance gas prices drop, Iran war ends after midterms: Ret. Lt. General
summary: MS Now segment with a retired general and analyst rejecting the president's claims that the economy is booming and gas will drop like a rock after the midterms.

assertions.quote: The country is booming, the country's booming.

verdicts.note: No operational definition; growth and jobs were positive while inflation, sentiment and real incomes were weak.

Real GDP grew at 2.5% and 2.2% annual rates in Q1 and Q2 2026, roughly trend growth, while payrolls averaged +45,000 a month and real hourly earnings fell 0.7% over the year; the economy is growing, but the data describe a solid expansion rather than a boom.

FOMC participants put longer-run real GDP growth at a 2.0% median (central tendency 2.0-2.2%) and project 2.3% for 2026, so 2026 growth runs only slightly above the economy's trend pace, an expansion rather than a boom.

assertions.quote: Gasoline's going to drop like a rock, just like it was just before.
THE NATIONAL AVERAGE FOR A GALLON OF DIESEL IS ALREADY THE HIGHEST IT'S EVER BEEN

verdicts.note: Gulf exports are distillate-heavy, so the Hormuz closure hit diesel hardest; the prior record was about $5.80 in June 2022.

assertions.quote: the price of gas, the price of all kinds of other things, having an impact on the politics of this country
